title: Chapter 2: Occupational Safety and Health in Workshops

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Workshop safety rules are divided into three primary categories: Personal Safety, General Safety, and Tool/Machine Safety.
Accidents in workshops primarily occur due to two factors: Unsafe Acts (human error) and Unsafe Working Conditions (faulty equipment or poor environment).
Safety signs are essential visual controls categorized into Prohibitory, Mandatory, Warning, and Information signs.
First aid awareness focuses on immediate life-saving care using the ABC principles: Airway, Breathing, and Circulation.
Adhering to proper Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) like safety goggles, boots, and helmets prevents severe personal injuries.

blocks.content: Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) refers to the measures and procedures used to protect workers from injuries, accidents, and health hazards in workplaces such as factories, workshops, construction sites, and industrial plants. In technical trades, workers regularly use machines, tools, electricity, and heavy materials, which can create dangerous situations if safety rules are not followed.
The main objective of occupational safety is to create a safe working environment where workers can perform their duties efficiently without risk to their health or life.

items: Prevent workplace accidents and injuries
Protect the health of workers
Ensure safe use of machines and tools
Improve productivity and efficiency
Reduce damage to machines and equipment
Promote a safety culture in the workplace

blocks.content: In workshops, workers operate cutting tools, electrical equipment, welding machines, and heavy machinery. If proper safety measures are not followed, serious accidents such as burns, electric shock, cuts, or machine injuries may occur.

cells: Safety measures protect workers from injuries and health hazards.
Proper operation prevents damage to expensive machines.
Safe workplaces allow workers to focus on their tasks.
Accidents can cause production loss and medical expenses.

Exam questions frequently ask about safety sign shapes and colors (e.g., Mandatory signs are blue circles; Warning signs are yellow triangles).
Definitions and examples distinguishing an 'Unsafe Act' from an 'Unsafe Condition' are common MCQs.
The exact expansion and order of 'ABC in First Aid' (Airway, Breathing, Circulation) is a high-frequency question.

blocks.content: First aid is the immediate assistance given to a person who has been injured or suddenly taken ill before professional medical help arrives.

items: Stop bleeding using clean cloth or bandage
Cool burns with clean water
Provide artificial respiration if necessary
Seek medical assistance immediately
Occupational Safety and Health focuses on protecting workers in workplaces.
Unsafe behavior and unsafe conditions are major causes of accidents.
Safety signs help workers identify hazards.
Both employers and workers share responsibility for safety.
